(b) Identify the conditions that must exist before performing CPR on a person, and explain how to recognize such conditions. Demonstrate the proper technique for performing CPR using a training device approved by your counselor.

pamphlet_excerpts: First aid for injuries or illnesses: Hyperventilation is the result of overbreathing, eitherdeliberately or because of panic (p. 21).
First aid for injuries or illnesses Principle 2: The likely result ofhyperventilation is dizziness and fainting, and victims willfeel as if they are being suffocated (p. 21).
First aid for injuries or illnesses Principle 3: Such a condition isunlikely in diving if the participants are properly prepared for each new skill level (p. 21).
First aid for injuries or illnesses Principle 4: If a diver shows signs of panicat any time, bring that person back into the boat or ontoshore, calm the person, and encourage slow breathing (p. 21).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (First aid for injuries or illnesses): Make sure the person rests in a comfortable position and has plenty of open, fresh air (p. 21).
Step 2 (First aid for injuries or illnesses): Before resuming anyactivity, find out and resolve the cause of the panic (p. 21).
Step 3 (First aid for injuries or illnesses): Ifyou feel sinus painwhile descending, stop your descent and end the dive (p. 21).
Step 4 (First aid for injuries or illnesses): A scuba diver may be injured by failing toequalize these air spaces, either while descending or ascending (p. 21).

Step 3 (BSA Swimmer Qualification Check): However, the in-water comfort level demonstrated by those who earn the Swimmingmerit badge is a better starting level for scuba training (p. 9).
Step 4 (BSA Swimmer Qualification Check): Your Scuba Diving merit badge instructor will specifywhat your Open Water Diver Certification prepares (p. 9).

Scuba Diver's Code Principle 4: The pressure on a diver's body increases with depth (p. 19).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Scuba Diver's Code): This increasein pressure causes nitrogen (the gas that makes up 79 percent of the air we breathe) to be absorbed into the body's tissues (p. 19).
Step 2 (Scuba Diver's Code): Thedeeper a diver dives and the longer the diver stays underwater, the more nitrogen the body absorbs (p. 19).
Step 3 (Scuba Diver's Code): The nitrogen that dissolves into a diver's tissues must leave the body as the diver exhales while ascending to the surface, or the diver (p. 19).
Step 4 (Scuba Diver's Code): To make sure that the excess nitrogen is properly and slowly released, diversshould always do the following. 1 (p. 19).
